The review range slider scrubs the recorded timeline in 40 ms steps, and RETURN TO SETTLED FIELD ends review.
A MARK SLOT button selects the recovered carrier in the settled field.
autonomous_processes: After arming, each carrier moves continuously by its seed-generated sine/cosine trajectory; the first target event begins at a generated 2700-3400 ms time and lasts 520 ms.
Eight later decoy events change other carriers on the generated schedule; the live phase continues until the generated settle time, then the browser autonomously switches to review.
Coordinate lens placement remains outcome-affecting during live and review, while the review slider and settled-slot selection remain available after the live field ends.
grouped_control_modes: Simplified coordinate-controls identity-lens observations during live or review across all seeds and attempts.
Simplified settled_slot_button carrier selection after RETURN TO SETTLED FIELD.
Review-spool navigation and return-to-settled transition for the recorded field.

clause_i.reason: For the candidate live lens-observation mode, a fixed action-and-time policy cannot identify the seed-generated first carrier and its moving position across histories; the required pre-change and change hits are target-position-specific.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded recent visual window can expose the lens-enlarged carrier glyph and reversible effect, and the same visible timeline can be inspected through the review control; this is sufficient visual evidence for choosing a lens observation, although it is not necessary during the live interval.

clause_iii.reason: Waiting through the live first change does not strictly reduce the value of the lens action: the review slider can rewind to the recorded first event, the browser renders that moving position and effect again, and the grader accepts observations whose mode is review. The first-change opportunity is therefore replayable rather than expiring.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: The candidate process is continuous carrier motion, a 520 ms first reversible visual change, and eight later reversible decoys. It is visible through the lens during live or review, but the complete timeline remains scrub-replayable after settlement, so this same process does not make an outcome-affecting opportunity degrade with waiting.

pre_run.reason: A solution can arm the field, send no outcome-affecting lens actions while the autonomous live phase runs, and then use the review slider to revisit the first event and collect the required pre-change and change observations before returning to the settled field. The browser permits review observations and the grader counts them, so this pre-run construction applies to every generated instance; no empirical percentage is needed.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 uses 9 carriers, eight decoys, a 520 ms first change, 54 px lens, three required change hits, two required pre-hits, and two occluders [236,286] and [468,522]; simplified mode uses coordinate and slot-button controls, and the shared observation window is 600 ms with 6 frames.

The generator creates moving carriers, chooses the first target from the visible set at first-change time, schedules eight later decoys, and stores settle, review, and proof timing in the public timeline.

The browser renders motion and occlusion, records observations in both live and review phases, automatically enters review at settlement, and binds simplified mode to coordinate lens placement and settled-slot buttons.

The grader binds simplified observations and selection to coordinate_controls and settled_slot_button, accepts observation mode live or review, and enforces the profile, proof counts, and target identity.

The implementation's solver confirms the review interface sequence and the distinct simplified coordinate/slot path; its private-state reads are treated only as implementation evidence, not as policy information.
